condition: single 2 cm mildly itchy red mosquito bite papule on right calf after lake camping
level_rationale: A single 2 cm red bump on the right calf today that itches mildly 2 days after a mosquito bite while camping by a lake is an uncomplicated local insect-bite reaction appropriate for over-the-counter anti-itch cream self-care, whereas the same 2 cm red bite bump on the calf that throbs with sharp pain 2 days after the bite indicates a localized painful inflammatory or secondary bacterial lesion requiring an outpatient doctor evaluation.

Has a 2 cm red bump at the bite site today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care dermatologic register swap ('erythematous papule today with mild pruritus' vs 'red bump today that itches mildly') + single-fact local sensory quality escalation control (-cf, mild itch to sharp throbbing pain, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 29, 1 mosquito bite on the right calf while lake camping 2 days ago, a 2 cm red bump today, and mild itchiness) with no diagnosis label or dialect lexicon term in any text and an exact 6-word vs 6-word continuous span swap. Replacing only fact f4 ('that itches mildly' to 'that throbs with sharp pain') keeps the localized 2 cm calf lesion intact while shifting care one step from over-the-counter anti-itch cream (level 1) to outpatient physician evaluation for a painful localized skin lesion (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5 and Rules A and D) with zero stated negatives.
